question: What is the primary goal of aseptic technique in nursing practice?

options.A: Eliminating all water in the room
options.B: Speeding up the patient discharge process
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital stays

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed practices that keep patients free from harmful disease-causing microbes during care. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: How does aseptic technique differ from everyday household cleaning?

options.A: Aseptic technique is only performed by medical doctors
options.B: Aseptic technique aims for the complete absence of disease-producing microbes
options.C: Household cleaning uses stronger bleach solutions than hospitals
options.D: Household cleaning is regulated by strict international health laws

explanation: While cleaning removes visible dirt, aseptic technique specifically targets invisible pathogens to protect patients during vulnerable procedures. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: Medical asepsis is also commonly referred to by which term?
explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on reducing the number of microbes and is widely known as clean technique in daily nursing tasks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h2)

question: A nurse is preparing to insert an indwelling urinary catheter. Which type of technique must be used?
explanation: Catheterization enters the sterile urinary tract, requiring surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria into the bladder. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h2)

question: What happens when a sterile item touches a non-sterile surface?

options.B: It is safe to use if dry
options.C: It can be wiped with alcohol to fix it
options.D: It remains sterile for one hour

explanation: The moment a sterile object touches anything not sterile, its sterile state is broken and it cannot be used. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why must sterile fields and items always be kept above waist level?

options.A: Hospital policies dictate that lower shelves are for waste
options.B: Gravity pulls heavier dust particles upward toward the chest
options.C: It prevents back strain during prolonged surgical procedures
options.D: Items below the waist are out of the nurse's direct line of sight

explanation: Anything below the waist or out of vision cannot be reliably monitored for contamination, so it is treated as unsterile. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infection?
explanation: Proper handwashing or alcohol rub use removes transient microbes from hands, preventing cross-contamination between patients. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed blood-borne viruses
options.B: Patients admitted to the surgical ward only
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.D: Individuals showing visible signs of a fever

explanation: Standard precautions assume any patient fluid could carry pathogens, protecting nurses and patients alike during every encounter. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which piece of personal protective equipment is put on last when preparing for a sterile procedure?
explanation: Gloves are always donned last so they remain clean and do not touch other equipment during the gowning and masking process. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of wearing a face mask and protective eyewear during certain procedures?

options.A: Keeping the nurse's face warm in cold operating rooms
options.B: Preventing the patient from seeing the nurse's facial expressions
options.C: Protecting mucous membranes from splashes of body fluids
options.D: Filtering out all oxygen molecules in the room

explanation: Masks and goggles create a barrier against blood or fluid splashes that could enter through the eyes, nose, or mouth. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which part of an opened sterile wrapper is considered non-sterile?

options.B: The inner contents of the tray
options.C: The top layer of the packaging
options.D: The exact center of the drape

explanation: The outer inch touches unsterile surfaces or hands when opening, making it unsafe to consider sterile. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why must a prepared sterile field never be left unattended by the nurse?

options.A: Sterile drapes have a tendency to blow away in room drafts
options.B: Contamination can occur unnoticed if no one is watching the field
options.C: Hospital security regulations forbid empty treatment rooms
options.D: Patients might try to steal the surgical instruments

explanation: Leaving a field unsupervised risks unseen breaches in sterility, which compromises patient safety if used. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h6)

question: A nurse is changing a dressing on a large surgical abdominal wound. What is the primary reason for using sterile instruments and supplies?

options.A: To make the dressing change process faster and easier
options.B: To prevent bacteria from entering the open surgical wound
options.C: To stop the patient from feeling pain during the procedure
options.D: To remove old scar tissue from previous operations

explanation: Open wounds are direct pathways for bacteria to cause local infection or systemic sepsis, making sterile tools essential. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h7)

question: What does the abbreviation HAI stand for in nursing practice?
explanation: HAIs are infections patients acquire while receiving medical treatment in a hospital or clinic facility. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which observation is an early sign of a localized wound infection that a nurse should report?

options.A: Normal pale pink skin around sutures

explanation: Pus and warmth around a wound site indicate active inflammation and bacterial infection requiring prompt intervention. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)
